name: Charter school independent study instructional funds
eligibility: Students enrolled in a public charter school's independent study/homeschool program that offers an instructional funds allotment. Not available to PSA, PSP or tutor homeschoolers.
benefit: A per-student budget set by each charter (not by statute) that the school spends on the family's behalf for curriculum, online courses, enrichment classes, lessons, and supplies from approved vendors. Amounts vary by school and grade and can change with the state budget; no official statewide figure exists. Charters receive LCFF funding (2026-27 base grants per ADA: $11,811 TK-3, $10,860 gr 4-6, $11,181 gr 7-8, $13,296 gr 9-12) subject to nonclassroom-based funding determinations.
how_to_apply: Enroll in the charter, sign the independent study master agreement, then submit purchase requests through the charter's ordering system/vendor list with your supervising teacher's approval.
california_notes: Ed Code 51747.3 bars a charter from claiming funding if it gives families funds or anything of value directly, so purchases go through the school and items may remain school property. Public funds cannot buy religious/sectarian materials (charters must be nonsectarian, Ed Code 47605); the challenge Woolard v. Thurmond (9th Cir. decision March 23, 2026) had a cert petition (No. 26-237) distributed for the U.S. Supreme Court's December 4, 2026 conference. Receiving charter funds disqualifies families from some private homeschool grants.

name: HSLDA Curriculum Grant (Compassion)
provider: Home School Legal Defense Association (HSLDA) Compassion / Homeschool Foundation
eligibility: Current HSLDA member; significant financial need; homeschooling at least one child age 6-19 for at least 3 months; funding homeschool privately (not receiving public funds, including ESAs or charter funds); legal custody; most schooling done at home with parent choosing the studies. Can be used for special learning needs resources.
benefit: About $300-$400 per child for curriculum and academic expenses (core curriculum, online class/co-op tuition, testing, tutoring, school-related technology).
how_to_apply: Apply online during an open window: Winter Jan 1-Feb 28, Spring Apr 1-Jun 30, Fall Sep 1-Oct 31 (windows can be shortened or cancelled depending on funds). One application per year; prior recipients submit receipts.
california_notes: California PSA and PSP families qualify; charter and district independent study families do not (public funds).

name: HSLDA Disaster Relief Grant
eligibility: Homeschool families recovering from natural disasters (details on the application page).
benefit: Help with emergency needs and replacement of homeschool goods after a disaster. Amount not published on the overview page.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Disaster Relief Grant application linked from hslda.org/grants.
california_notes: Relevant after California wildfires, floods and earthquakes.

name: HSLDA Membership Financial Aid
eligibility: Homeschool families who cannot afford HSLDA membership.
benefit: Free HSLDA membership, which also makes the family eligible to apply for the Curriculum Grant.
how_to_apply: Apply for Membership Financial Aid via HSLDA (linked from the Curriculum Grant page).
california_notes: Membership gives access to HSLDA's California legal guidance and sample letters.

name: 529 plan K-12 expenses (federal expansion under P.L. 119-21)
provider: Internal Revenue Code section 529 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act, P.L. 119-21, signed July 4, 2025)
eligibility: 529 account beneficiaries with expenses 'in connection with enrollment or attendance at an elementary or secondary public, private, or religious school' (IRC 529(c)(7)).
benefit: Federally tax-free K-12 withdrawals now cover: tuition; curriculum and curricular materials; books or other instructional materials; online educational materials; tutoring or educational classes outside the home by an unrelated qualified tutor (licensed teacher, former eligible-institution teacher, or subject-matter expert); fees for nationally standardized norm-referenced achievement tests, AP exams and college admission exams; dual enrollment fees; and educational therapies for students with disabilities by licensed/accredited practitioners. Expanded expenses apply to distributions after July 4, 2025. Annual K-12 cap rises from $10,000 to $20,000 per beneficiary for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025 (i.e., 2026 onward).
how_to_apply: Open or use any state's 529 plan; withdraw for qualified K-12 expenses and keep receipts. Report on federal return (Form 1099-Q).
california_notes: The statute does not use the word 'homeschool'; whether a California home-based private school (legally a private school under Ed Code 48222/33190) qualifies is a matter for a tax adviser and IRS guidance. Tutoring must be 'outside the home' and by an unrelated tutor. California does NOT conform: see the ScholarShare entry.

name: California tax treatment of K-12 529 withdrawals / ScholarShare 529
provider: ScholarShare Investment Board / California Franchise Tax Board
eligibility: California taxpayers using any 529 plan (including ScholarShare 529) for K-12 expenses.
benefit: None at the state level for K-12: California has not conformed to the federal K-12 529 rules (since 2018), so the earnings portion of K-12 withdrawals is subject to California income tax plus an additional 2.5% state tax. California also gives no state deduction for 529 contributions. Withdrawals for qualified higher education remain state tax-free.
how_to_apply: Report K-12 withdrawal earnings as income on the California return (FTB Schedule CA / Form 5805 for the 2.5% additional tax); consult a tax professional.
california_notes: The 2025 federal expansion (expanded K-12 categories, $20k limit) does not change California treatment. Pending California bills have not changed K-12 conformity as of Nov 2026 (verify for the current tax year).

name: Coverdell Education Savings Account (ESA)
eligibility: Beneficiary under 18 when contributions are made (or special needs); contributor income limits apply (phase-out traditionally $95,000-$110,000 MAGI single, $190,000-$220,000 joint).
benefit: Up to $2,000 per beneficiary per year in total contributions; earnings tax-free federally when used for qualified elementary and secondary expenses (tuition, books, supplies, equipment, academic tutoring, computer/internet, special needs services) at a 'school' as determined under state law, as well as higher education.
how_to_apply: Open a Coverdell ESA with a bank or brokerage; withdraw for qualified expenses and keep receipts.
california_notes: Because a California home-based private school is a private school under state law, homeschool K-12 expenses may qualify; confirm with a tax adviser. California state tax conformity for Coverdell K-12 withdrawals not confirmed online; check FTB guidance.

name: Federal Tax Credit Scholarship program (Educational Choice for Children, IRC 25F)
provider: U.S. Treasury/IRS via state-approved Scholarship Granting Organizations (SGOs)
eligibility: Donors: individual federal taxpayers. Students: K-12 students in households up to 300% of area median income in states that opt in, through SGOs listed by the state.
benefit: Starting January 1, 2027, a dollar-for-dollar federal tax credit of up to $1,700 per taxpayer per year ($3,400 married filing jointly per advocacy summaries) for donations to SGOs, which fund K-12 scholarships for qualified education expenses.
how_to_apply: Families would apply to an SGO in their state once the state opts in and lists SGOs; donors claim the credit on their federal return.
california_notes: As of late October 2026 Governor Newsom had NOT announced whether California will opt in; the opt-in for tax year 2027 is due by January 1, 2027 (with SGO lists by Feb 15 per reporting). ACR-229 urges opt-in. About 31 states had opted in. If California does not opt in, Californians can still donate to out-of-state SGOs but California students cannot receive these scholarships. Whether homeschool expenses would be covered depends on federal definitions and SGO rules. Re-check status after Jan 1, 2027.

name: Community college special admit (concurrent enrollment) with fee exemption
eligibility: K-12 students recommended by their school principal (for a PSA homeschool, the parent-principal) and with parental consent, admitted as special part-time or full-time students (Ed Code 76001, 48800, 48800.5). Colleges set grade/age, placement and course limits.
benefit: College credit that also counts on the high school transcript. Governing boards may exempt special part-time students (up to 11 units) from the enrollment fee (Ed Code 76300(f)) and they are exempt from nonresident tuition; many districts waive enrollment fees for special part-time students. Special full-time students typically pay fees but may qualify for the California College Promise Grant.
how_to_apply: Submit the CCCApply application plus the college's K-12 special admit/concurrent enrollment form signed by the principal and parent each term.
california_notes: Fee waivers are discretionary and vary by district; homeschool (PSA) students generally use the special admit route rather than CCAP. Under the 2025 federal 529 changes, dual enrollment fees are a qualified K-12 expense federally (not for California tax).

name: College and Career Access Pathways (CCAP) dual enrollment
provider: California Community Colleges in partnership with school districts/charters
eligibility: High school students attending a school district, county office or charter school that has a CCAP partnership agreement with a community college district (Ed Code 76004). Charter and district IS students may qualify through their school; PSA/PSP students generally are not covered.
benefit: Up to 15 units per term; enrollment and student representation fees waived and no fee may be charged that Ed Code 49011 prohibits; priority registration; courses often free of textbook costs per local agreement.
how_to_apply: Ask the charter or district high school counselor which CCAP courses are offered and complete the partnership's enrollment steps.
california_notes: CCAP is created by AB 288 (2015) and was extended/expanded by later bills (e.g., AB 30, 2019). Availability depends entirely on the local partnership.

name: California College Promise Grant (community college enrollment fee waiver)
eligibility: California residents (or AB 540 eligible) meeting income standards, receiving qualifying public assistance, or with financial need per FAFSA/CADAA.
benefit: Waives the per-unit enrollment fee at any California community college.
how_to_apply: Apply via the FAFSA/California Dream Act Application or the College Promise Grant application at the college.
california_notes: Useful for homeschool graduates starting at a community college and, in some districts, for special full-time high school students not covered by special admit fee exemptions.

name: SAT fee waivers (including homeschoolers)
eligibility: Low-income 11th-12th graders (e.g., eligible for free/reduced-price lunch, household income within USDA limits, public assistance). Homeschooled students are eligible.
benefit: Free SAT registrations (typically two), free score sends, and college application fee waivers at participating colleges.
how_to_apply: Homeschoolers may request a waiver directly from College Board via the SAT Fee Waiver Request Form (signed into a College Board account) with proof of eligibility, or through a local high school counselor.
california_notes: Homeschoolers register and test at a public test center.

name: AP Exam fee reduction
eligibility: Students with significant financial need. Homeschooled students may receive the same reductions as other students.
benefit: College Board fee reduction of $37 per AP Exam (schools may also waive their portion); some states add subsidies.
how_to_apply: Homeschoolers arrange to test through the AP coordinator at a school that offers AP exams (contact AP Services for Students for a list); the coordinator applies the reduction.
california_notes: California does not currently offer a separate state AP exam fee subsidy for homeschoolers (not confirmed). Find a host school early in the fall.

name: PSAT/NMSQT for homeschoolers (National Merit Scholarship entry)
provider: College Board / National Merit Scholarship Corporation
eligibility: Homeschooled students (taken in 11th grade for National Merit eligibility) testing at a local school that administers the PSAT/NMSQT.
benefit: Entry into the National Merit Scholarship Program and other scholarship programs; low-income students may receive fee waivers through the host school.
how_to_apply: Contact local high schools months ahead (summer) to arrange to test as a homeschooled student.
california_notes: Arrange with a nearby public or private school; availability of seats varies.

name: Every Kid Outdoors 4th grade pass
provider: U.S. Department of the Interior, USDA Forest Service and partner federal agencies
eligibility: U.S. 4th graders including homeschooled students (and free-choice learners age 10).
benefit: Free entry for the 4th grader and accompanying family (one vehicle at per-vehicle sites) to national parks, forests, wildlife refuges and other federal lands and waters, valid through August 31 of the school year (2026-27 pass valid through August 31, 2027). Does not cover camping or other amenity fees.
how_to_apply: Complete the short online activity at everykidoutdoors.gov and print the voucher (can be exchanged/converted to a digital pass via Recreation.gov).
california_notes: Covers Yosemite, Sequoia/Kings Canyon, Joshua Tree, Death Valley, Redwood, Channel Islands etc. Homeschoolers ARE eligible (unlike the California state parks 4th grade pass).

name: California State Parks Free Fourth Grade Pass (formerly Adventure Pass)
provider: California Department of Parks and Recreation
eligibility: California PUBLIC school 4th graders only (program funded by Proposition 98). Charter and district independent study students are public school students; PSA/PSP homeschool students are NOT eligible.
benefit: Free day-use entry to 54 participating state parks for the student and family, valid up to 13 months (through August 31 of the following year).
how_to_apply: Parent/guardian applies through ReserveCalifornia.com (account required) once sign-up opens in August.
california_notes: Renamed from 'Adventure Pass' (launched 2021 with 19 parks). For PSA/PSP families, use the library parks pass or the federal Every Kid Outdoors pass instead.

name: California State Library Parks Pass
provider: California State Library and California State Parks, via local public libraries
eligibility: Anyone who can check out materials from a participating California public library (no special card needed).
benefit: Free vehicle day-use entry (one vehicle up to 9 people) at 200+ participating state park units; loan period set by each library.
how_to_apply: Place a hold on/check out the Parks Pass from your local public library.
california_notes: Originally a pilot; reporting in 2026 indicates ongoing funding was secured, but confirm with your library. Not valid at units run by other agencies or concessionaires; parking not guaranteed.

name: Discover & Go museum passes
provider: Participating California public library systems (e.g., LA County, San Diego, San Francisco, San Jose, Fresno, Santa Clara County)
eligibility: Adult library cardholders (usually 18+) residing in the library's service area; rules vary by library.
benefit: Free or discounted passes to museums, science centers, zoos and cultural attractions.
how_to_apply: Log in to your library's Discover & Go portal with your card and reserve a pass (typically up to 2 active reservations).
california_notes: Excellent for field trips; combine with homeschool days offered by many museums.

name: Apple education pricing for homeschool teachers
eligibility: Apple's U.S. education terms list homeschool teachers among eligible K-12 educators.
benefit: Education pricing on Macs, iPads and selected accessories (purchase limits apply).
how_to_apply: Buy through the Apple Education Store; Apple may request qualifying information (a copy of your PSA filing is commonly used as proof).
california_notes: Barnes & Noble's former Educator discount (which included homeschool parents) ENDED April 12, 2023; many websites still advertise it. Other retailer teacher discounts vary and change frequently, so verify before relying on them.

name: California LifeLine (phone) and LifeLine Home Broadband Pilot
eligibility: Households enrolled in qualifying programs (e.g., Medi-Cal, CalFresh, LIHEAP) or with income at or below program limits (June 1, 2026-May 31, 2027: $24,600 for 1 person, $33,300 for 2, $42,100 for 3, +$8,700 each additional).
benefit: Discounted home/cell phone service; the Home Broadband Pilot (launched January 26, 2026, three years) gives $20/month off home internet or $30/month off bundled internet+phone with participating providers.
how_to_apply: Apply through California LifeLine (via a participating provider/LifeLine Administrator), then ask a participating ISP to apply the broadband discount. Since Feb 1, 2026, California LifeLine and federal Lifeline require separate enrollments.
california_notes: Replaces some of the help lost when the federal Affordable Connectivity Program ended in 2024.

name: Cal Grant (for homeschool graduates)
eligibility: California residents (or AB 540) with financial need within income/asset ceilings. Cal Grant A generally needs a 3.0 GPA, Cal Grant B a 2.0. Homeschool graduates without a verifiable GPA may substitute accepted test scores (SAT, ACT, GED, HiSET, TASC) or a community college GPA (16+ units).
benefit: Tuition/fee awards at UC, CSU and eligible private colleges; access/living allowance; community college awards.
how_to_apply: File the FAFSA or California Dream Act Application and submit GPA verification (or test scores) by March 2 of senior year (check CSAC for current deadlines and any deadline extensions for community colleges).
california_notes: A PSA home school can submit a GPA verification form as the school; otherwise use the test-score substitution. Keep the transcript and diploma ready.

name: Middle Class Scholarship
eligibility: California undergraduates (and teaching credential students) at UC, CSU or CCC bachelor's degree programs with family income and assets each up to the annual ceiling (e.g., $234,000 for 2025-26 per UC San Diego); FAFSA/CADAA required. No high school GPA requirement known.
benefit: Sliding-scale scholarship toward remaining cost of attendance based on income and other aid received.
how_to_apply: File the FAFSA or California Dream Act Application by the CSAC deadline; no separate application.
california_notes: Homeschool graduates are evaluated like other undergraduates once enrolled at UC/CSU.

name: Federal Student Aid (Pell Grant, etc.) for homeschool graduates
eligibility: Students who completed secondary school in a homeschool setting treated as a home or private school under state law are eligible for federal aid (20 U.S.C. 1091(d)).
benefit: Pell Grants, work-study and federal loans.
how_to_apply: File the FAFSA (opens October 1); indicate homeschool completion. Colleges may ask for a transcript or other completion evidence.
california_notes: A California PSA home school is a private school under Ed Code 48222, so graduates qualify.

name: Jack Kent Cooke Foundation College Scholarship
eligibility: High school seniors with unmet financial need (family income up to $95,000 considered), minimum unweighted GPA 3.75, SAT/ACT/AP/IB scores; homeschooled students are explicitly eligible.
benefit: One of the largest undergraduate scholarships in the U.S., covering a substantial share of college costs for up to four years, plus advising (check jkcf.org for the current maximum award).
how_to_apply: Online application, typically opening in August with a fall deadline.
california_notes: No state restriction.

name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
eligibility: Students 18 or younger as of the deadline (no minimum age; based on age, not grade) who complete a significant project in STEM, literature, music or philosophy; U.S. citizen or permanent resident. No school-type restriction found, so homeschoolers apply under the same rules.
benefit: Scholarships of $10,000, $25,000 or $50,000.
how_to_apply: Online application; the 2027 cycle opens fall 2026 with a February 2027 deadline (exact date to be posted by Davidson).
california_notes: Well suited to project-based homeschool learners.

name: No state-funded California homeschool grant or ESA
eligibility: N/A
benefit: California has no education savings account, voucher, or state grant program for private homeschoolers (PSA/PSP). Public funding reaches homeschooling families only through enrollment in charter or district independent study.
how_to_apply: N/A
california_notes: Watch for a California decision on the federal tax-credit scholarship program (opt-in deadline January 1, 2027).
